Netflix is the largest entertainment platform on Earth, and the single most important battleground for what your family watches. The VirtueVigil database now holds 57 Netflix originals with completed Woke Scores, and the picture they paint is clearer than any one show can convey on its own. This is the full list, ranked from most woke to most traditional.

The spread is enormous. At the top sits Emilia Pérez at a -25.4 margin (STRONGLY WOKE). At the bottom sits Happy Gilmore 2 at a +27.8 margin (STRONGLY TRADITIONAL). That is a 53-point range within a single platform, which tells you Netflix is not one thing. It is a collection of teams with wildly different instincts, and the difference between what one team makes and another team makes is the difference between a lecture and a movie.

The shape of the distribution matters. Two titles land STRONGLY WOKE, twelve WOKE LEAN, and nine MIXED, with a striking absence: not a single Netflix original lands in the plain WOKE tier between -10 and -20. Netflix tends to either go fully woke or stay in the lean zone. On the other side, seventeen titles land TRADITIONAL LEAN, eleven TRADITIONAL, and six STRONGLY TRADITIONAL. That is 34 titles leaning traditional or stronger against 14 leaning woke or stronger. The raw numbers are not the story, though. The story is which titles those are.

The pattern that jumps out first: prestige drama and animated kids' content cluster on the woke side, while action, thriller, and legacy franchise content clusters on the traditional side. Emilia Pérez, Glass Onion, Adolescence, and Bridgerton are awards machines and algorithm darlings, and they are also the most ideologically aggressive. Extraction, War Machine, Peaky Blinders, and Cobra Kai are the shows Netflix makes when it wants a broad, durable audience, and they lean hard the other way. Parents do not need a decoder ring to navigate this. They need the scores. Here they are, ranked from most woke to most traditional.

STRONGLY WOKE (Margin -20.0 and Below)

#1: Emilia Pérez (2024)

Woke Score: 30.4 • Traditional Score: 5.0 • Verdict: STRONGLY WOKE • Margin: -25.4

Genre: Musical / Crime / Drama | Platform: Netflix

Emilia Pérez is the most woke title in the entire Netflix catalog by a wide margin. Jacques Audiard's Spanish-language musical about a Mexican cartel boss who transitions is a stylistic experiment bolted onto a progressive thesis: identity is the only true redemption, and the traditional institutions around it, family, church, the state, are the obstacles. The 30.4 woke score reflects a film that wears its ideology in every scene. The 5.0 traditional score reflects a film that has almost nothing left over for story, character, or the ordinary moral texture audiences connect with. It swept awards-season attention precisely because of what it is. That is the point worth knowing.

#2: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery (2022)

Woke Score: 24.3 • Traditional Score: 4.0 • Verdict: STRONGLY WOKE • Margin: -20.3

Genre: Mystery / Comedy | Platform: Netflix | Director: Rian Johnson

Rian Johnson's second Benoit Blanc mystery replaces the first film's class critique with a blunt and literal one: the villain is a tech billionaire who lies, cheats, and destroys people, and the heroes are the ensemble of clever outsiders who take him down. The mystery structure is real and the craft is high, which is why the traditional score is not zero. But the film's moral engine runs entirely on resentment of wealth and status, and it never once complicates that premise. At 24.3 woke to 4.0 traditional, this is a whodunit that knows exactly who it thinks is guilty before the first body drops.

WOKE LEAN (Margin -0.1 to -9.9)

#3: Enola Holmes 3 (2026)

Woke Score: 16.1 • Traditional Score: 7.4 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -8.7

Genre: Mystery / Adventure | Platform: Netflix | Director: Philip Barantini

The Enola Holmes franchise has always carried its feminism on its sleeve, and the third installment does not break form. Enola's cleverness is framed as the correction to her brother's institutional arrogance, and the film consistently positions the establishment as the thing standing between young women and their freedom. The mystery craft and the genuine warmth between the Holmes siblings keep the traditional score alive, but the ideological direction has never been in doubt.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Enola Holmes 3

#4: Adolescence (2025)

Woke Score: 22.5 • Traditional Score: 14.8 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -7.8

Genre: Psychological Crime Drama | Platform: Netflix

Adolescence is the rare show where both scores run high, because it is genuinely interested in something real: what turns a child into a killer. The woke side comes from the show's insistence that the answer lies in toxic masculinity, online radicalization, and a culture that fails boys. The traditional side comes from the show's unflinching willingness to hold a family accountable and to treat the crime as a tragedy rather than a systemic abstraction. It is ambitious television that never quite separates diagnosis from ideology, which is why it lands WOKE LEAN rather than MIXED.

#5: Bridgerton: Season 4 (2026)

Woke Score: 16.2 • Traditional Score: 10.0 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -6.2

Genre: Regency Romance Drama | Platform: Netflix

Bridgerton sells itself as romance and delivers progressive messaging through its casting, its sexual politics, and its constant reframing of Regency society as a system of oppression that the good characters chafe against. The show's romance engine and its commitment to happy endings keep the traditional score in double digits, which is exactly why it is so effective as an ideological delivery vehicle. Audiences come for the love story and absorb the framing by osmosis.

#6: KPop Demon Hunters (2025)

Woke Score: 22.6 • Traditional Score: 16.7 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -5.9

Genre: Animated Musical Urban Fantasy | Platform: Netflix

This animated musical about K-pop idols who hunt demons is a fascinating case: it carries heavy woke freight in its identity politics and its treatment of fame and gender, but its demon-hunting premise is built on a fundamentally traditional good-versus-evil frame that keeps the traditional score surprisingly high. The result is a kids' title with a real ideological tug-of-war inside it, and parents should know which direction it leans.

#7: Squid Game: Season 3 (2025)

Woke Score: 18.7 • Traditional Score: 12.9 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -5.8

Genre: Survival Thriller / Dystopian Drama | Platform: Netflix | Director: Hwang Dong-hyuk

Squid Game was always a class critique dressed as a survival thriller, and by the third season the critique has hardened into a full-throated indictment of wealth, inequality, and the people who profit from desperation. The traditional score survives because the show still believes in sacrifice, loyalty, and the moral weight of choosing to do the right thing under pressure. But the show's answer to who is to blame has never been subtle, and it is not meant to be.

#8: Wednesday: Season 2 (2025)

Woke Score: 21.1 • Traditional Score: 15.4 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -5.7

Genre: Gothic Mystery / Dark Comedy | Platform: Netflix

Wednesday Addams has always been an outsider figure, and the modern series leans into that outsider status as a vehicle for identity-first storytelling. The second season keeps the gothic charm and the murder-mystery structure, but it sharpens the framing around female defiance of patriarchal and institutional authority. The traditional score stays elevated because the Addams family itself is built on loyalty and love, which is the show's saving grace and its most confusing feature for parents trying to sort it out.

#9: Red Notice (2021)

Woke Score: 8.5 • Traditional Score: 2.8 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -5.7

Genre: Action / Comedy / Heist | Platform: Netflix | Director: Rawson Marshall Thurber

Red Notice is an odd case: a star-vehicle heist comedy that carries a surprisingly low traditional score. The film's banter-driven plot never builds real stakes or real loyalty between its characters, and the woke lean comes less from an explicit agenda than from a general cynicism about authority and a surface-level girlboss framing of its female lead. It is not a film with a thesis. It is a film where the absence of a traditional moral center quietly shows.

#10: Wednesday (2022)

Woke Score: 16.1 • Traditional Score: 10.6 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -5.5

Genre: Supernatural Mystery Comedy | Platform: Netflix

The first season of Wednesday established the template that the sequel would follow: a heroine defined by her refusal to conform, a school that stands in for every institution she is supposed to submit to, and a mystery that rewards her defiance. The Addams family warmth is present from the start, which keeps the traditional score alive, but the show's core argument, that the system is the enemy and the misfit is the hero, lands squarely in the woke-lean zone.

#11: Stranger Things (2025)

Woke Score: 13.0 • Traditional Score: 8.0 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -5.0

Genre: Sci-Fi & Fantasy | Platform: Netflix

The Stranger Things franchise is a study in drift. The first season was a loving, mostly traditional homage to 1980s coming-of-age adventure. By the later seasons the show had layered in heavier progressive framing around its characters' identities while keeping the monster-fighting core intact. This entry reflects the franchise as a whole: still fundamentally a story about friendship and courage, but increasingly freighted with contemporary identity messaging that pulls it left of center.

#12: All Quiet on the Western Front (2022)

Woke Score: 13.9 • Traditional Score: 9.0 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -4.9

Genre: War / Drama | Platform: Netflix | Director: Edward Berger

This is a war film that hates war, and that hatred is what produces its woke lean: the film's anti-war argument bleeds into an anti-military, anti-authority framing that treats the generals and the state as the enemy as much as the opposing army. The traditional score survives because the film is fundamentally about the brotherhood of soldiers and the horror of what war does to young men, which is a deeply traditional subject even when the politics around it tilt progressive.

The Electric State is built on a familiar progressive template: the robots are the sympathetic outsiders, the corporation is the villain, and the human institutions are the thing the heroes must escape. The road-trip warmth between its leads gives the film a genuine traditional heartbeat, but the film's worldview, that technology's casualties are the good guys and the system that created them is the enemy, is woke-lean through and through.

Woke Score: 9.0 • Traditional Score: 5.0 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -4.0

Genre: Thriller | Platform: Netflix

Ozark is a show about a family dragged into crime, and its moral center is the casualty. The Byrdes' gradual corruption is framed less as individual moral failure than as the inevitable result of a system that rewards the ruthless, which is what pushes the show's lean. The traditional score stays low because the show never really believes in redemption, family loyalty, or institutional legitimacy, only survival. It is gripping television with a hollow moral core.

The Takeaway

Netflix is not a monolith, and anyone who says otherwise is not looking at the data. The same platform that greenlit Emilia Pérez also greenlit Apollo 13. The same executives who ordered Adolescence also ordered Cobra Kai. The difference between a -25.4 margin and a +27.8 margin is not a subtle shading. It is the difference between two entirely different companies occupying the same app.

The pattern is clear enough to be useful. Prestige drama and animated kids' content skew woke. Action, thriller, and legacy franchise content skew traditional. If you are choosing what to watch with your family, the bottom half of this list is where the real stories live, and the top half is where the messaging lives. That is not a value judgment from us. It is what the scores show.

Two titles deserve special mention. Emilia Pérez, at -25.4, is the most woke thing Netflix has ever made, a film where the ideology is the product and the story is the wrapper. And Happy Gilmore 2, at +27.8, is the most traditional, a film where family is the product and everything else is decoration. Those two poles define the platform. Everything else on this list is a point on the line between them.

The absence in the middle is telling. Not a single Netflix original lands in the plain WOKE tier between -10 and -20. Netflix does not do moderation, not on the woke side. It either goes all the way or it stays in the lean zone. Parents should know which side of that line any given title falls on before they press play. That is what this list is for.
